scenarios.title: Canonical schema materializes the audit substrate refusals depend on
scenarios.purpose: Confirm the database the product builds actually contains security_events and audit_events, the only tables where a refused release can be durably recorded. If either is absent, the 'every refusal is recorded' criterion is impossible regardless of handler logic.
scenarios.rationale: AC-4 (every refusal recorded) is only meaningful if a durable audit table exists in the canonical schema the release path writes to.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-AUTHZ-2 AC 'every refusal is recorded in the audit log'

actions.name: canonical schema table list
actions.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import sqlite3,tempfile,os,sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src'); from freight_recon.schema import create_canonical_schema; p=os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(),'probe.sqlite3'); c=sqlite3.connect(p); create_canonical_schema(c); print(sorted(r[0] for r in c.execute(\"select name from sqlite_master where type='table'\")))"

scenarios.isolation_note: Builds a throwaway schema in a fresh tempdir; touches no shared DB or port, so it cannot contaminate any other scenario.

assumptions: The local app at 127.0.0.1:8001 is the run_action_callback_server callback service (service_refs: callback) bound to the driver_probe workspace DB at data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3.
Release of an operation is realized through the signed-action / operation-approval intake in action_callback.py; there is no separate unsigned 'release' HTTP endpoint.
The server is running when request-based scenarios execute; if it is not, those scenarios will fail on connection rather than on product behavior.
'security_events' is the recording table for authorization refusals at the transport boundary and 'audit_events' for run-scoped decisions, per phase2_tenant_first.py.
A refused release never carries actor='system' into a 'slack_operation_started' event, making that count an invariant zero usable as a 'no release occurred' oracle.
unresolved_questions: What is the concrete release contract the builder added? The task names an 'operator console' but the console in-repo (operator_console.py) is a static HTML page; the only live release path requires a Slack- or delivery-signed token. No release endpoint that takes a supervisor identity in a driveable form is visible.

How is 'supervisor' represented and checked? The canonical schema (schema.py, phase2_tenant_first.py) has no roles table or role column, and code today authorizes by Slack user/channel allowlist. Without a persisted role model, the supervisor/non-supervisor distinction (AC-1, AC-2) cannot be authoritatively evaluated.

AC-1 (a supervisor CAN release) is not verifiable with the approved commands: none of them can mint a valid signed release token, and run_action_callback_server hardwires operation_router=None so the approval path is inert/unreachable. A signed-token fixture or a supervisor-authenticated release endpoint is needed to exercise the happy path.

AC-3 (cross-tenant supervisor cannot release another tenant's operation) is not exercisable: it requires two provisioned tenants each with a valid supervisor release token. Note workflow.py:906 documents that release_operation_commit is NOT tenant-qualified — this should be reviewed as a likely cross-tenant defect.

Does a refused release on the /actions/signed and /email/action routes actually write to security_events/audit_events? Those handlers (handle_signed_action_callback) return 401/400 but appear NOT to record, unlike the Slack operation-approval route — a probable AC-4 gap that needs a token-minting fixture to confirm end to end.

Is a before/after audit-log delta observable? With single approved sqlite commands and no ability to snapshot-then-compare, 'a NEW refusal row was written by THIS request' cannot be asserted precisely; only invariant properties (e.g. system actor never starts an operation) are robust.
